title: Schema lifecycle curator and incremental type-signal router for usage ingestion
creator: Priya Raman
description: Introduce a small, opinionated service (Schema Lifecycle Curator) that owns per-tenant schema versions, soft-coercion rules, and a lightweight type-signal router that annotates incoming usage events with resolved type hints. The goal is to reduce hard rejections caused by minor shape drift, provide deterministic feature flags for strict vs lenient ingestion, and emit telemetry so console teams can see mismatch rates and corrective actions. This ticket implements core reconciliation, an HTTP/gRPC onramp for the existing ingest mesh, and a short-term compatibility shim for downstream consumers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New Curator service deployed to staging and wired to ingest mesh; 2) Incoming events annotated with type signals and a schema_version header; 3) Configurable leniency per-tenant (strict/lenient/auto-correct) exposed via config service; 4) Mismatch rate metrics appear in Grafana dashboard with breakdown by tenant and route; 5) End-to-end test bath for common shape drift cases; 6) No increase in 5xx ingest error rate >0.2% during canary.
implementation_notes: - Build as a small Rust service to keep CPU and memory footprint low; - Use an internal lightweight registry (Redis-backed) for current schema pointers and soft-coercion rules; - On cache miss, consult long-term store (Postgres) and mark an eventual async reconcile; - Annotate events with a 3-bit type-signal (OK, COERCED, REJECTED) and attach a short reason code; - Emit structured telemetry for decisions (decision, rule_id, tenant, route, latency).
migration_plan: Phase 1: Staging-only routing via feature flag; Phase 2: Canary on 5% of production traffic for low-risk tenants; Phase 3: Gradual ramp with rollback flag. Provide a one-click migration dashboard to preview tenant mismatch history and allow opt-in to lenient mode. Maintain a fallback path that returns original event unchanged when the curator is unreachable.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy service to staging and run integration harness against synthetic shapes; 2) Canary on internal tenants + low-volume customers for 48h; 3) Expand to 20% traffic if mismatch rate stable; 4) Full rollout with monitoring alerts and automated rollback on elevated rejection or latency regressions.
metrics:
- ingest.schema.mismatch_rate (per-tenant, per-route)
- ingest.schema.coercion_rate
- ingest.curator.latency.p50/p95/p99
- ingest.curator.cache_hit_rate
- downstream.consumer.rejection_rate_change
comments: 2025-01-28 Priya Raman: Initial ticket created after spike with Console SRE — observed 0.8% of ingestion rejections attributable to small shape drift. Proposed dedicated curator instead of expanding the ingest mesh to keep runtime simple.

2025-02-05 Evan Chen: Proto design review completed. Decided on Redis cache with Postgres fallback. Concern raised about eventual consistency for rapid schema updates — resolved via write-through invalidation and version tombstones.
2025-02-18 Marisol Ortega (PM): Requested an explicit migration dashboard and tenant preview UI. Added to scope but kept as low-touch first iteration (link-only preview).
2025-02-24 Engineering: Benchmarked Rust service locally; p95 latency for annotation under load is 6ms with cache hit. CPU footprint acceptable. Added circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures.
2025-03-01 Security Review: Security team requested a requirement to log schema changes and to audit who can change leniency flags. We will add ACL checks against IAM during phase 2.
2025-03-05 Evan Chen: Integration tests green in staging. Starting 2% production canary next week scoped to non-critical tenants. Created PR 1629 for service + adapter; docs in Confluence updated.
